subproblems.title: An approximate tangent plane forces Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = O(ρⁿ) (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let D ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set, x ∈ ℝ^P, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P and r₀ > 0 with Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x)) < ∞, where Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure) and B̄_r(z) is the closed ball. Suppose D has approximate tangent space Q at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n D x Q: dim Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(D)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as ρ ↓ 0, where η_{x,ρ}(y) = ρ⁻¹(y − x) and the integrals are Bochner integrals). Then there are C ∈ ℝ and r₁ > 0 such that Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Cρⁿ) for every ρ with 0 < ρ < r₁.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (D : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (r₀ : ℝ), MeasurableSet D → 0 < r₀ → μHE[n] (D ∩ closedBall x r₀) ≠ ∞ → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n D x Q → ∃ C r₁ : ℝ, 0 < r₁ ∧ ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < r₁ → μHE[n] (D ∩ closedBall x ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * ρ ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3) (chapter-03.txt lines 91–95), with an explicit test function. Notation: μ := μHE[n]; B̄_r(z) is the closed ball; for ρ > 0, η_ρ(y) := ρ⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x ρ), a homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse z ↦ x + ρz; ∫_S f dμ denotes the Bochner integral of f against μ⌞S.

1. Scaling. Let ρ > 0 and Z ⊆ ℝ^P. Then η_ρ(Z) = ρ⁻¹ • (Z − x), where Z − x := {z − x : z ∈ Z}. μ is translation invariant (μHE[n] is add-right-invariant on ℝ^P), so μ(Z − x) = μ(Z); and μ(c • W) = |c|ⁿ μ(W) for every c ≠ 0 and every W ⊆ ℝ^P (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). Hence μ(η_ρ(Z)) = ρ^{−n} μ(Z). Moreover, for R > 0, η_ρ(Z) ∩ B̄_R(0) = η_ρ(Z ∩ B̄_{Rρ}(x)), because |ρ⁻¹(z − x)| ≤ R ⟺ |z − x| ≤ Rρ. Therefore
   (1a) μ(η_ρ(Z) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = ρ^{−n} μ(Z ∩ B̄_{Rρ}(x)) for all Z ⊆ ℝ^P, ρ > 0, R > 0.
If Z is Borel then so is η_ρ(Z), η_ρ being a homeomorphism.

2. Test function. Put f(y) := max(0, min(1, 2 − |y|)). Then f is continuous, 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f = 1 on B̄_1(0) and f = 0 outside B̄_2(0); since B̄_2(0) is compact (finite dimension), f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). In particular 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ f ≤ 1_{B̄_2(0)} pointwise.

3. Integrability. Let 0 < ρ ≤ r₀/2. By (1a) with R = 2, μ(η_ρ(D) ∩ B̄_2(0)) = ρ^{−n} μ(D ∩ B̄_{2ρ}(x)) ≤ ρ^{−n} μ(D ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x)) < ∞. Since |f| ≤ 1_{B̄_2(0)}, f is integrable with respect to μ⌞η_ρ(D). Also 1_{B̄_1(0)} is integrable with respect to μ⌞η_ρ(D), because μ(η_ρ(D) ∩ B̄_1(0)) ≤ μ(η_ρ(D) ∩ B̄_2(0)) < ∞.

4. Lower bound. For 0 < ρ ≤ r₀/2, monotonicity of the integral (steps 2 and 3) and (1a) with R = 1 give
   ∫_{η_ρ(D)} f dμ ≥ ∫_{η_ρ(D)} 1_{B̄_1(0)} dμ = μ(η_ρ(D) ∩ B̄_1(0)) = ρ^{−n} μ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)),
all quantities being finite real numbers (μ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ μ(D ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x)) < ∞).

5. Limit. By the hypothesis HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n D x Q applied to f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_ρ(D)} f dμ → L := ∫_Q f dμ ∈ ℝ as ρ ↓ 0. Choose r₁ with 0 < r₁ ≤ r₀/2 such that ∫_{η_ρ(D)} f dμ ≤ L + 1 for all 0 < ρ < r₁.

6. Conclusion. Put C := L + 1. For 0 < ρ < r₁, steps 4 and 5 give ρ^{−n} μ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ C; multiplying by ρⁿ > 0, the finite quantity μ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) is at most Cρⁿ, i.e. μ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Cρⁿ). For n = 0 every step holds verbatim (ρ⁰ = 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: Scaling: Hⁿ(η_{x,ρ}(Z) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = ρ^{−n}Hⁿ(Z ∩ B̄_{Rρ}(x)) by translation invariance and euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀.
Test function f = max(0, min(1, 2 − |y|)) ∈ C_c with 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ f ≤ 1_{B̄_2(0)}, integrable on η_{x,ρ}(D) for ρ ≤ r₀/2.
ρ^{−n}Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(D)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ =: L.
Hence Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ (L + 1)ρⁿ for all small ρ > 0.

subproblems.title: Locality of approximate tangent planes for nested Borel sets (Simon Ch. 3, Remarks 1.5(2), 1.8(1))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let A ⊆ B ⊆ U be Borel sets with Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A (that is, for μHE[n]⌞A-almost every x) the following holds simultaneously for every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P: B has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q, Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4) if and only if A has approximate tangent space Q at x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remarks 1.5(2) and 1.8(1), chapter-03.txt lines 86–90 and 298–305; density theorem Ch. 1, Theorem 3.16, chapter-01.txt lines 905–925). The parent's nested sets B ⊆ C ⊆ A are renamed here: the small set is A, the large set is B, and the parent's ambient locally finite set is taken to be B itself. Notation: μ := μHE[n]; B̄_r(z), B_r(z) are the closed and open balls; for ρ > 0, η_ρ(y) := ρ⁻¹(y − x) (blowUpMap x ρ); all integrals are Bochner integrals.

1. Countable compact cover. Let 𝒟 ⊆ ℝ^P be a countable dense set and 𝒥 := {(c, r) ∈ 𝒟 × ℚ : r > 0, B̄_r(c) ⊆ U}, a countable set. For j = (c, r) ∈ 𝒥 put K_j := B̄_r(c), a compact subset of U. Every y ∈ U lies in the open ball B_r(c) for some (c, r) ∈ 𝒥: choose ε > 0 with B̄_ε(y) ⊆ U (U is open), c ∈ 𝒟 with |y − c| < ε/3 and a rational r with ε/3 < r < 2ε/3; then |y − c| < r, and for |z − c| ≤ r we get |z − y| ≤ r + |y − c| < ε, so B̄_r(c) ⊆ B̄_ε(y) ⊆ U.

2. Density theorem. For j ∈ 𝒥 let λ_j := μ⌞(B ∩ K_j). Its total mass μ(B ∩ K_j) is finite by hypothesis, so λ_j is a finite, hence locally finite, Borel measure on ℝ^P. Besicovitch's density theorem (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.16; Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div, valid on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P) applied to λ_j and the set A gives: for λ_j⌞A-a.e. x, λ_j(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/λ_j(B̄_ρ(x)) → 1 as ρ ↓ 0 (quotients in [0, ∞]). Since A ⊆ B, λ_j⌞A = μ⌞(A ∩ K_j), so there is a μ-null set N_j such that this convergence holds at every x ∈ (A ∩ K_j) ∖ N_j. Put N := ⋃_{j∈𝒥} N_j, a μ-null set (𝒥 is countable).

3. Local notation. Fix x ∈ A ∖ N. As x ∈ A ⊆ U, step 1 gives j = (c, r) ∈ 𝒥 with x ∈ B_r(c); put δ₀ := (r − |x − c|)/2 > 0, so B̄_{δ₀}(x) ⊆ B_r(c) ⊆ K_j. Then x ∈ (A ∩ K_j) ∖ N_j, so the quotient of step 2 tends to 1. For 0 < ρ ≤ δ₀ and every Z ⊆ B we have λ_j(Z ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = μ(B ∩ K_j ∩ Z ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = μ(Z ∩ B̄_ρ(x)). Write a(ρ) := μ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) and b(ρ) := μ(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x)); both are finite for ρ ≤ δ₀ (they are at most μ(B ∩ K_j)), and b(ρ)/a(ρ) → 1 as ρ ↓ 0.

4. Small excess relative to a(ρ). For each ε ∈ (0, 1) there is ρ_ε ∈ (0, δ₀] such that μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ε·a(ρ) for 0 < ρ < ρ_ε. Indeed, choose ρ_ε with b(ρ)/a(ρ) > 1 − ε for 0 < ρ < ρ_ε. Then a(ρ) > 0 (if a(ρ) = 0 then b(ρ) = 0 and the quotient is 0/0 = 0 in [0, ∞]), hence b(ρ) ≥ (1 − ε)a(ρ). Since A ⊆ B and all quantities are finite, μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = a(ρ) − b(ρ) ≤ ε·a(ρ).

5. Growth of a(ρ) and vanishing excess density. Suppose that A or B has an approximate tangent space at x, and let D ∈ {A, B} be such a set, with tangent space Q. D is Borel and μ(D ∩ B̄_{δ₀}(x)) ≤ a(δ₀) < ∞, so the sibling lemma tangent_growth (applied with r₀ := δ₀) gives K₀ ∈ ℝ and r₁ > 0 with μ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(K₀ρⁿ) for 0 < ρ < r₁; replacing K₀ by max(K₀, 0) we may assume K₀ ≥ 0, so μ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ K₀ρⁿ for 0 < ρ < r₁. If D = B, then a(ρ) ≤ K₀ρⁿ for 0 < ρ < r₁. If D = A, then for 0 < ρ < min(r₁, ρ_{1/2}) step 4 gives a(ρ) = b(ρ) + μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ K₀ρⁿ + a(ρ)/2, hence (a(ρ) being finite) a(ρ) ≤ 2K₀ρⁿ. In both cases there are K ≥ 0 and r₂ > 0 with a(ρ) ≤ Kρⁿ for 0 < ρ < r₂. Combining with step 4: for every ε ∈ (0, 1), μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ εKρⁿ for 0 < ρ < min(r₂, ρ_ε). Hence
   (†) ρ^{−n} μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.

6. Comparison of blow-ups. Assume (†). Let g ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), choose R ≥ 1 with g = 0 outside B̄_R(0), and put M_g := sup|g| < ∞. Let 0 < ρ < δ₀/R. As in step 1 of tangent_growth, μ(η_ρ(Z) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = ρ^{−n} μ(Z ∩ B̄_{Rρ}(x)) for every Z (translation invariance and μ(cW) = |c|ⁿμ(W)). Hence μ(η_ρ(B) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = ρ^{−n} a(Rρ) < ∞, so g is integrable on η_ρ(B) and on its Borel subsets η_ρ(A) and η_ρ(B ∖ A). Since η_ρ is injective, η_ρ(B) is the disjoint union of η_ρ(A) and η_ρ(B ∖ A), and therefore
   ∫_{η_ρ(B)} g dμ − ∫_{η_ρ(A)} g dμ = ∫_{η_ρ(B∖A)} g dμ,
   |∫_{η_ρ(B∖A)} g dμ| ≤ M_g μ(η_ρ(B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = M_g ρ^{−n} μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_{Rρ}(x)) = M_g Rⁿ (Rρ)^{−n} μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_{Rρ}(x)),
which tends to 0 as ρ ↓ 0 by (†) (Rρ ↓ 0). Thus ∫_{η_ρ(B)} g dμ − ∫_{η_ρ(A)} g dμ → 0.

7. Conclusion. Let x ∈ A ∖ N and let Q be a linear subspace. If HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q, then dim Q = n, step 5 applies with D = B, and by step 6, for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_ρ(A)} g dμ = ∫_{η_ρ(B)} g dμ + o(1) → ∫_Q g dμ; hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q. Conversely, if HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q, then step 5 applies with D = A and step 6 gives ∫_{η_ρ(B)} g dμ → ∫_Q g dμ for every g, so HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q. The null set N does not depend on Q, and μ⌞A(N) = 0; hence the equivalence holds for μ⌞A-a.e. x and all Q simultaneously. For n = 0 the argument is unchanged. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cover U by countably many compact balls K_j ⊆ U whose interiors cover U.
Besicovitch density theorem for the finite measures Hⁿ⌞(B ∩ K_j): Hⁿ(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/Hⁿ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) → 1 for a.e. x ∈ A.
Hence Hⁿ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ε Hⁿ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) for small ρ.
If A or B has a tangent plane at x, tangent_growth gives Hⁿ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = O(ρⁿ), so Hⁿ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = o(ρⁿ).
Then |∫_{η(B)} g − ∫_{η(A)} g| ≤ sup|g| ρ^{−n}Hⁿ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_{Rρ}(x)) → 0, so the limits in Definition 1.4 coincide.

subproblems.title: Tangent planes and orientations of an IMRep transfer to Borel supersets of subsets of its carrier
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in U (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient), and let B, C be Borel sets with B ⊆ M, B ⊆ C ⊆ U and Hⁿ(C ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ B there is a linear subspace Q of ℝ^P such that C has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q) and ξ(x) is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U B C : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet B → MeasurableSet C → B ⊆ R.carrier → B ⊆ C → C ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (C ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict B), ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the double application of the locality lemma in steps 3 and 5 of the parent proof. Notation: μ := μHE[n], M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient.

1. M is locally finite in U. M is Borel and M ⊆ U (fields measurableSet_carrier, carrier_subset). For compact K ⊆ U, θ ≥ 1 on M (θ is ℕ-valued and positive on M by mult_pos), so μ(M ∩ K) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} 1 dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dμ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult.

2. Apply the sibling lemma tangent_locality with open set U, small set B and large set M: B ⊆ M ⊆ U are Borel and M is locally finite in U by step 1. Hence for μ⌞B-a.e. x, for every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q.

3. Apply tangent_locality with open set U, small set B and large set C, using the hypotheses on B and C. Hence for μ⌞B-a.e. x, for every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q.

4. The field orients of R says: for μ⌞M-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Since B ⊆ M we have μ⌞B ≤ μ⌞M, so this also holds for μ⌞B-a.e. x.

5. Let x lie outside the union of the three μ⌞B-null exceptional sets of steps 2–4. Take Q from step 4. By step 2 (⟹), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q; by step 3 (⟸), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q; and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. This proves the claim for μ⌞B-a.e. x. ∎
proof_key_steps: The carrier M of an IMRep is Borel and locally Hⁿ-finite in U because θ ≥ 1 on M.
tangent_locality for B ⊆ M and for B ⊆ C: a.e. on B, T_xB = T_xM and T_xB = T_xC.
The orients field of R holds a.e. on B ⊆ M; combine to get T_xC = T_xM oriented by ξ(x).

subproblems.title: Two unit orientations of the same n-plane differ by a sign
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P and let v, w ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n: continuous linear functionals on n-covectors, ⟨α, v⟩ = v(α)). If v and w are both unit orientations of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf v Q and IsUnitOrientationOf w Q: for some orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P spanning Q, v(α) = ±α(τ) and w(α) = ±α(τ') for all n-covectors α), then w = v or w = −v.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v w : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf v Q → IsUnitOrientationOf w Q → w = v ∨ w = -v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the linear-algebra part of step 3 of the parent proof (orthonormal bases of Q differ by an orthogonal matrix of determinant ±1).

1. Unfolding the hypotheses: there are orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q = span(range τ'), and signs ε, ε' ∈ {1, −1} with v(α) = ε·α(τ) and w(α) = ε'·α(τ') for every n-covector α (continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ).

2. Each τ_i and τ'_i lies in Q, so τ, τ' may be regarded as families in the inner product space Q, where they are still orthonormal. Since τ is linearly independent and spans Q, dim Q = n; an orthonormal (hence linearly independent) family of n vectors in the n-dimensional space Q spans Q. Hence τ and τ' are orthonormal bases b and b' of Q indexed by Fin n.

3. Let d := det_b(b'), the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix from b to b'. Both bases are orthonormal, so this matrix is orthogonal and d ∈ {1, −1} (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real).

4. Let α be an n-covector and α_Q its restriction to Q (α composed with the inclusion Q → ℝ^P in each slot), an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space Q. Every such form is a multiple of det_b: α_Q = α_Q(b)·det_b (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α(τ') = α_Q(b') = α_Q(b)·det_b(b') = d·α(τ). The number d does not depend on α.

5. Hence for every α: w(α) = ε'·α(τ') = ε'd·α(τ) = (εε'd)·(ε·α(τ)) = s·v(α), where s := εε'd ∈ {1, −1} (using ε² = 1). Therefore w = s·v, i.e. w = v if s = 1 and w = −v if s = −1. For n = 0 the same argument applies (τ = τ' is the empty family, Q = {0}, d = 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: Both orthonormal families spanning Q are orthonormal bases b, b' of Q.
det_b(b') = ±1 because the change-of-basis matrix is orthogonal.
For every n-covector α, α(τ') = det_b(b')·α(τ) since alternating n-forms on Q are multiples of det_b.
Therefore w = (εε'det_b(b'))·v with εε'det_b(b') ∈ {±1}.

subproblems.title: Orientations of two IMReps agree up to sign a.e. on the overlap of their carriers
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁), R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂) be IMReps in U (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]): ξ₂(x) = ξ₁(x) or ξ₂(x) = −ξ₁(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R₁ R₂ : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R₁.carrier ∩ R₂.carrier)), R₂.orient x = R₁.orient x ∨ R₂.orient x = -R₁.orient x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 (agreement on the overlap) of the parent proof. Notation: μ := μHE[n].

1. M₂ is Borel, M₂ ⊆ U, and for compact K ⊆ U, μ(M₂ ∩ K) ≤ ∫⁻_{M₂∩K} θ₂ dμ < ∞ (θ₂ ≥ 1 on M₂ by mult_pos; locallyIntegrable_mult). The set M₁ ∩ M₂ is Borel, contained in M₁ and in M₂.

2. Apply the sibling lemma imrep_tangent_transfer with R := R₁, B := M₁ ∩ M₂, C := M₂ (hypotheses: step 1). So for μ⌞(M₁ ∩ M₂)-a.e. x there is Q₁ with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ x Q₁ and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ₁ x) Q₁.

3. The field orients of R₂ holds μ⌞M₂-a.e., hence μ⌞(M₁ ∩ M₂)-a.e. (M₁ ∩ M₂ ⊆ M₂): there is Q₂ with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ x Q₂ and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ₂ x) Q₂.

4. Let x be outside both exceptional null sets. Approximate tangent spaces are unique (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1); SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so Q₁ = Q₂. Thus ξ₁(x) and ξ₂(x) are unit orientations of the same subspace, and the sibling lemma orientation_sign gives ξ₂(x) = ξ₁(x) or ξ₂(x) = −ξ₁(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: M₂ is Borel and locally Hⁿ-finite in U.
imrep_tangent_transfer (R₁, B = M₁ ∩ M₂, C = M₂): a.e. on M₁ ∩ M₂, ξ₁ orients T_xM₂.
The orients field of R₂: a.e. on M₁ ∩ M₂, ξ₂ orients T_xM₂; uniqueness of T_xM₂.
orientation_sign: ξ₂ = ±ξ₁.

subproblems.title: An IMRep whose weighted orientation is p₁θ₁ξ₁1_{M₁} + p₂θ₂ξ₂1_{M₂} a.e.
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁), R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂) be IMReps in U (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1) and p₁, p₂ ∈ ℤ. Then there is an IMRep R = (M', θ', ξ') in U such that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) the n-vectors satisfy 1_{M'}(x)θ'(x)ξ'(x) = p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ₂(x) (written with Set.indicator and scalar multiplication in MultiVector P n).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R₁ R₂ : IMRep U n) (p₁ p₂ : ℤ), IsOpen U → ∃ R : IMRep U n, ∀ᵐ x ∂μHE[n], R.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R.mult y : ℝ) • R.orient y) x = (p₁ : ℝ) • R₁.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₁.mult y : ℝ) • R₁.orient y) x + (p₂ : ℝ) • R₂.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₂.mult y : ℝ) • R₂.orient y) x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–5 of the parent proof. Notation: μ := μHE[n]; M_i := R_i.carrier, θ_i := R_i.mult, ξ_i := R_i.orient; A := M₁ ∪ M₂, a Borel subset of U; sgn : ℤ → {−1, 0, 1} is the sign; for an integer c, |c| ∈ ℕ is its absolute value. For compact K ⊆ U, μ(M_i ∩ K) ≤ ∫⁻_{M_i∩K} θ_i dμ < ∞, because θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i (mult_pos) and by locallyIntegrable_mult.

1. Borel orientations. ξ_i is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M_i, so there is a strongly measurable (Borel) ξ̃_i : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) with ξ̃_i = ξ_i μ⌞M_i-a.e. (Mathlib AEStronglyMeasurable.mk / ae_eq_mk). Equivalently: for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ M_i ⇒ ξ̃_i(x) = ξ_i(x).

2. Borel sign on the overlap. Define σ(x) := 1 if ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) and σ(x) := −1 otherwise. The set {ξ̃₂ = ξ̃₁} is Borel (both maps are strongly measurable into the metrizable space Λ_n(ℝ^P)), so σ : ℝ^P → ℤ is Borel. Claim: for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ ⇒ ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x). Indeed, by the sibling lemma overlap_orientation_sign and step 1, for μ⌞(M₁ ∩ M₂)-a.e. x we have ξ̃₁(x) = ξ₁(x), ξ̃₂(x) = ξ₂(x) and ξ₂(x) = ±ξ₁(x), hence ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) or ξ̃₂(x) = −ξ̃₁(x). In the first case σ(x) = 1; in the second case, if ξ̃₂(x) ≠ ξ̃₁(x) then σ(x) = −1 and ξ̃₂(x) = −ξ̃₁(x), while if ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) we are in the first case. In all cases ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x). (This equality test replaces the parent proof's coordinate test Σ_I⟨e^I, ξ₁⟩⟨e^I, ξ₂⟩ ≥ 0, whose verification needs the Cauchy–Binet identity; only the property ξ̃₂ = σξ̃₁ a.e. on M₁ ∩ M₂ is used below.)

3. Coefficient and orientation field. Define c : ℝ^P → ℤ and ζ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) by
   c(x) := p₁θ₁(x)1_{M₁}(x) + p₂θ₂(x)(σ(x)1_{M₁∩M₂}(x) + 1_{M₂∖M₁}(x)),   ζ(x) := ξ̃₁(x) if x ∈ M₁, ζ(x) := ξ̃₂(x) otherwise.
c is Borel (ℤ is countable with the discrete σ-algebra; c is built from the Borel maps θ₁, θ₂, σ and the indicators of the Borel sets M₁, M₂), ζ is strongly measurable (piecewise on the Borel set M₁), c = 0 off A, and since at most one of 1_{M₁∩M₂}(x), 1_{M₂∖M₁}(x) is nonzero and |σ| = 1,
   (3a) |c(x)| ≤ |p₁|θ₁(x)1_{M₁}(x) + |p₂|θ₂(x)1_{M₂}(x) for all x.

4. Pointwise identity. Let x satisfy [x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ ⇒ ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x)]. Then p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ̃₂(x) = c(x)ζ(x). Cases: if x ∉ A both sides are 0; if x ∈ M₁ ∖ M₂ both sides equal p₁θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x); if x ∈ M₂ ∖ M₁ both sides equal p₂θ₂(x)ξ̃₂(x); if x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ the left side is p₁θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x) + p₂θ₂(x)σ(x)ξ̃₁(x) = (p₁θ₁(x) + p₂θ₂(x)σ(x))ξ̃₁(x) = c(x)ζ(x).

5. Definition of R. Let M' := {x ∈ A : c(x) ≠ 0}, θ'(x) := |c(x)| ∈ ℕ and ξ'(x) := sgn(c(x))·ζ(x). Since |c|·sgn(c) = c, and c(x) = 0 whenever x ∉ M' (either x ∉ A, or x ∈ A with c(x) = 0), we have
   (5a) 1_{M'}(x)θ'(x)ξ'(x) = c(x)ζ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P.

6. R = (M', θ', ξ') is an IMRep in U:
   (a) M' is Borel (A and c are Borel) and M' ⊆ A ⊆ U.
   (b) M₁ ∪ M₂ is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion applied to the sequence M₁, M₂, M₂, …), hence so is M' ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
   (c) θ' = |c| is Borel and θ' ≥ 1 on M'.
   (d) For compact K ⊆ U, by (3a): ∫⁻_{M'∩K} θ' dμ ≤ |p₁|∫⁻_{M₁∩K} θ₁ dμ + |p₂|∫⁻_{M₂∩K} θ₂ dμ < ∞.
   (e) ξ' is strongly measurable (product of the Borel real function sgn∘c and ζ), hence AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M'.
   (f) Orientation. M' is Borel, M' ⊆ U, and μ(M' ∩ K) ≤ μ(M₁ ∩ K) + μ(M₂ ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. Apply the sibling lemma imrep_tangent_transfer with R := R₁, B := M' ∩ M₁, C := M': for μ-a.e. x ∈ M' ∩ M₁ there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ₁ x) Q; for a.e. such x also ξ̃₁(x) = ξ₁(x) (step 1), so ξ'(x) = sgn(c(x))ξ₁(x) with sgn(c(x)) = ±1 (c(x) ≠ 0 on M'). A unit orientation multiplied by −1 is a unit orientation of the same plane (same τ, the other sign alternative), so IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ' x) Q. Likewise apply imrep_tangent_transfer with R := R₂, B := M' ∖ M₁ (⊆ M₂ because M' ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂), C := M': for μ-a.e. x ∈ M' ∖ M₁ there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q, IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ₂ x) Q and ξ'(x) = sgn(c(x))ξ̃₂(x) = ±ξ₂(x). Since M' = (M' ∩ M₁) ∪ (M' ∖ M₁), the orients property holds μ⌞M'-a.e.

7. The identity. By steps 1 and 2, for μ-a.e. x: (i) x ∈ M_i ⇒ ξ̃_i(x) = ξ_i(x) for i = 1, 2, and (ii) x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ ⇒ ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x). At every such x, (5a), step 4 and (i) give
   1_{M'}(x)θ'(x)ξ'(x) = c(x)ζ(x) = p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ̃₂(x) = p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ₂(x)
(the indicator 1_{M_i}(x) vanishes when x ∉ M_i). This is the asserted identity, μ-a.e. ∎
proof_key_steps: Replace ξ₁, ξ₂ by Borel versions ξ̃₁, ξ̃₂ equal to them a.e. on M₁, M₂.
Borel sign σ := 1 on {ξ̃₂ = ξ̃₁}, −1 elsewhere; by overlap_orientation_sign, ξ̃₂ = σξ̃₁ a.e. on M₁ ∩ M₂.
c := p₁θ₁1_{M₁} + p₂θ₂(σ1_{M₁∩M₂} + 1_{M₂∖M₁}), ζ := ξ̃₁ on M₁, ξ̃₂ off M₁; then p₁1_{M₁}θ₁ξ̃₁ + p₂1_{M₂}θ₂ξ̃₂ = cζ.
M' := {c ≠ 0} ∩ (M₁ ∪ M₂), θ' := |c|, ξ' := sgn(c)ζ satisfy every IMRep field; orientation via imrep_tangent_transfer on M' ∩ M₁ and M' ∖ M₁.
1_{M'}θ'ξ' = cζ everywhere, hence equals p₁1_{M₁}θ₁ξ₁ + p₂1_{M₂}θ₂ξ₂ a.e.

subproblems.title: An a.e. identity of weighted orientations yields the integer combination of the represented currents
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁), R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂), R = (M, θ, ξ) be IMReps in U (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1) and p₁, p₂ ∈ ℤ. Suppose that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) the n-vectors satisfy 1_M(x)θ(x)ξ(x) = p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ₂(x). Then for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (ω : TestFormOn U n) we have τ(R)(ω) = p₁τ(R₁)(ω) + p₂τ(R₂)(ω), where τ(R)(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R₁ R₂ R : IMRep U n) (p₁ p₂ : ℤ), (∀ᵐ x ∂μHE[n], R.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R.mult y : ℝ) • R.orient y) x = (p₁ : ℝ) • R₁.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₁.mult y : ℝ) • R₁.orient y) x + (p₂ : ℝ) • R₂.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₂.mult y : ℝ) • R₂.orient y) x) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) = (p₁ : ℝ) * R₁.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) + (p₂ : ℝ) * R₂.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof. Notation: μ := μHE[n]; for an IMRep R' = (M', θ', ξ') put F_{R'}(x) := 1_{M'}(x)θ'(x)ξ'(x) ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P), so the hypothesis reads F_R = p₁F_{R₁} + p₂F_{R₂} μ-a.e. Fix a test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U): ω is smooth, hence continuous, with compact support K := tsupport ω ⊆ U; put W := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞ (operator norm on n-covectors), and note ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ K.

1. Norm bound. If v is a unit orientation of some Q, i.e. v(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal τ, then |v(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ |α|·∏_i|τ_i| = |α| for every n-covector α (operator norm bound of continuous alternating maps, Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).

2. Integrability. Let R' = (M', θ', ξ') be any IMRep in U. The function h(x) := θ'(x)ξ'(x)(ω(x)) is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M' (θ' is Borel; ξ' is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M'; ω is continuous; the evaluation map (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous). By the field orients and step 1, for μ⌞M'-a.e. x, |h(x)| ≤ θ'(x)|ω(x)| ≤ W θ'(x)1_K(x). The bound is integrable on M': its integral is W∫⁻_{M'∩K} θ' dμ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult (K is compact and K ⊆ U). Hence h is integrable on M'.

3. Rewriting the action. For an IMRep R' as in step 2 and every x, F_{R'}(x)(ω(x)) = 1_{M'}(x)h(x). As M' is Borel, R'.action ω = ∫_{M'} h dμ = ∫_{ℝ^P} F_{R'}(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x), and x ↦ F_{R'}(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable by step 2.

4. Conclusion. Evaluating the hypothesis at ω(x): F_R(x)(ω(x)) = p₁F_{R₁}(x)(ω(x)) + p₂F_{R₂}(x)(ω(x)) for μ-a.e. x. Integrating over ℝ^P (integrals of a.e.-equal functions agree; linearity of the Bochner integral for the integrable functions x ↦ F_{R_i}(x)(ω(x)) of step 3) and using step 3 three times:
   R.action ω = ∫ F_R(ω) dμ = p₁∫ F_{R₁}(ω) dμ + p₂∫ F_{R₂}(ω) dμ = p₁ R₁.action ω + p₂ R₂.action ω. ∎
proof_key_steps: A unit orientation v satisfies |v(α)| ≤ |α|.
θ'ξ'(ω) is integrable on the carrier of every IMRep, dominated by sup|ω|·θ'1_{spt ω}.
R'.action ω = ∫ (1_{M'}θ'ξ')(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x).
Integrate the a.e. identity evaluated at ω(x) and use linearity of the integral.
